correctness.rationale: For R_{m,n}=L(K_{m,n}), a selected line-graph induced forest is exactly a union of vertex-disjoint alternating paths and isolated original vertices. Paths with endpoints on opposite sides contribute (uv)^r z^(2r-1); paths with endpoints in one side contribute (u+v)(uv)^r z^(2r)/2; exponential formula with isolated vertices gives exp(u+v+wuv(z+(u+v)z^2/2)/(1-uvz^2)). The maximum edge count is min(a+b-1,2a) by forest and small-side degree bounds; alternating spanning paths attain it. Equality forces either an alternating Hamilton path for a=b or every small-side vertex of degree 2 if a<b; exact composition/binomial extraction gives the claimed N_{a,b,k}. Independent exhaustive subsets for m,n=(2,3),(2,4),(3,3),(3,4) confirm the enumerator and extremal histogram (R_{2,4}: 24 connected, 6 two-component). Infinite theorem is symbolic.
